title: Plano's Jashan Becomes First D-FW Indian Restaurant With a Michelin Nod
excerpt: Michelin's 2026 Texas update added Plano's Jashan to its Recommended list — a first for an Indian restaurant in Dallas-Fort Worth — while Goldee's Barbecue earned Fort Worth's first-ever star.
body:
• Jashan, an Indian fine-dining restaurant at 7401 Lone Star Drive, Suite B120 in Plano's Legacy North complex, was added to the Michelin Guide's Recommended list in the 2026 Texas update announced Oct. 8, 2026 — the first Indian restaurant in Dallas-Fort Worth history to earn a Michelin nod.
  • Chef Ramesh Thangaraj was recruited from a Michelin-recognized restaurant in Malaysia; the tasting menu narrates the history of Indian cuisines around an open demonstration kitchen, with à la carte plus a shorter tasting in the main dining room.
  • If you're going: the full tasting experience sits in the demo-kitchen room, while the main dining room keeps it shorter and à la carte. Jashan is just off the Dallas North Tollway, in a space owner Prasanna Singaraju — a tech-industry worker — found empty in a parking garage.
  • The nod signals Michelin is finally looking at the suburbs north of Dallas, as the guide faces pressure to step up its North Texas research before local tourism boards decide whether to renew its contract.

The suburbs north of Dallas cook some of the best Indian food in Texas, and the Michelin Guide has mostly acted like they don't exist. That changed Oct. 8, 2026, when the guide's 2026 Texas update added Jashan — the Plano Indian fine-dining restaurant — to its Recommended list. It is the first Indian restaurant in Dallas-Fort Worth history to earn a Michelin nod.

The Recommended designation means Jashan was selected by Michelin's anonymous inspectors for the quality of its food; it carries no star and no Bib Gourmand. For a suburban Indian restaurant, though, the line on Michelin's list is the breakthrough.

Context & Background

Jashan opened in Plano's Legacy North shopping complex in a suite its owner found in a parking garage near the Dallas North Tollway. Owner Prasanna Singaraju, who works in the tech industry, recruited chef Ramesh Thangaraj from a Michelin-recognized restaurant in Malaysia — one cited as Malaysia's best newcomer of 2023.

The format is unusual. The tasting menu is a narrative of the history of Indian cuisines, served around an open demonstration kitchen. The main dining room offers à la carte plus a shorter tasting menu. D Magazine's April 2026 profile called it an only-in-Texas story, and the magazine's October guide piece now puts Jashan ahead of its non-Michelin rival Sanjh.

The 2026 update wasn't only Jashan's moment. Other new Recommended additions: Fond on Elm Street in downtown Dallas, Mābo, a Japanese yakitori spot in Park Cities, and Olōyō, a contemporary Mexican restaurant on Gaston Avenue in East Dallas.

Impact & Analysis

North Texas had its biggest Michelin day yet. Goldee's Barbecue in Fort Worth earned its first star — the city's first-ever star — and two more stars went to Austin restaurants. Mamani and Tatsu Dallas retained their stars. North Texas now counts three starred restaurants, the most it has ever held, though Houston and Austin still dominate the list.

The full Texas count: 19 starred restaurants statewide, none at the two- or three-star level. On the Bib Gourmand side, Resident Taqueria — a small chef-driven taco shop on Audelia Road in Lake Highlands — earned its first Bib. Lucia in Bishop Arts lost its Bib and moved to the Recommended list.

The guide faces pressure to step up North Texas research before local tourism boards decide whether to renew its contract — a backdrop that makes Jashan's inclusion look like more than coincidence.

Diaspora Angle

For Indian diners in North Texas, the recognition is a correction as much as an award. Plano, Frisco, and Irving are where much of the region's Indian community lives and eats, and the guide's long indifference to that cooking has been a sore point. A Plano Indian restaurant on Michelin's list is a correction as much as an award.

There is pedigree behind it too. Thangaraj came from a Michelin-recognized kitchen in Malaysia, cited as the country's best newcomer of 2023 — a reminder that Indian fine dining's talent pipeline is global, and suburban Texas kitchens are drawing from it.

What's Next

The question now is whether Jashan climbs. Recommended is Michelin's entry tier; a star — or even a Bib Gourmand — would put a Plano Indian restaurant alongside Goldee's and Tatsu Dallas.

Michelin itself has decisions to make. Tourism boards in North Texas are weighing whether to renew the guide's contract, and the 2026 update — with a Plano Indian restaurant and a Fort Worth barbecue joint sharing the spotlight — looks like the guide's answer. Whether it is enough will be decided at the negotiating table, not the tasting table.
